---
title: "Getting started"
---

## 1. Build

```bash
go build -o wraptool .
```

On Guix systems, the bundled manifest gives you a reproducible
toolchain:

```bash
guix shell -m manifest.scm -- go build -o wraptool .
```

## 2. Create a config

`wraptool` reads YAML from `~/.config/wraptool/config.yaml` (XDG, with
`--config` / `WRAPTOOL_CONFIG` overrides).

```yaml
server:
  transport: sse
  listen: 127.0.0.1:8717

tools:
  git:
    binary: /usr/bin/git
    timeout: 30s
    allow:
      - subcommand: [status]
        flags: ["--short", "--branch", "--porcelain"]
      - subcommand: [log]
        flags: ["--oneline", "-n", "--format", "--graph"]
        flag_constraints:
          "-n": { type: integer, max: 100 }
      - subcommand: [diff]
        flags: ["--stat", "--name-only", "--staged"]
      - subcommand: [commit]
        flags: ["--message", "--amend"]
        flag_constraints:
          "--message": { required: true }
      - subcommand: [push]
        flags: ["--set-upstream"]
        deny_flags: ["--force", "--force-with-lease"]
    deny:
      - subcommand: [remote, set-url]
```

See [Configuration reference](configuration.qmd) for every field.

## 3. Start the server

```bash
wraptool serve
```

The available transports:

| Transport | Config | Use case |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| `stdio`   | `transport: stdio` | Harness launches wraptool directly |
| `sse`     | `transport: sse`, `listen: host:port` | Independent process, TCP |
| `unix`    | `transport: unix`, `listen: /path/to.sock` | Independent process, Unix socket |

For SSE and Unix transports, add an auth token:

```yaml
server:
  transport: sse
  listen: 127.0.0.1:8717
  auth_token_file: ~/.config/wraptool/auth_token
```

```bash
head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64 > ~/.config/wraptool/auth_token
```

## 4. Connect your coding assistant

```bash
wraptool init --harness claude --harness cursor --url http://127.0.0.1:8717/sse
```

This writes the MCP config block for each harness. Supported values:
`claude`, `cursor`, `opencode`, `gemini`, `roo`, `windsurf`, or `all`.

## 5. Smoke test

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
  participant AI as AI assistant
  participant W  as wraptool
  participant G  as git
  AI->>W: tools/call git_status
  W->>W: policy.Evaluate
  W->>G: exec /usr/bin/git status
  G-->>W: stdout
  W->>W: scrub credentials
  W-->>AI: ToolResult
```

Trigger any allowed subcommand from your assistant. The wraptool log
prints one line per executed command with status and duration.
